Neeva identity

Need + Value, built on thoughtful choice.

The Neeva logo expresses the relationship between need and value in a warm, human way. It is more than a mascot: every element stands for a part of the problem we are solving.

Our problem space is impulse buying. Neeva is not an anti-shopping app. It never shames the user. It gives people a short, calm pause at the moment of checkout, so the next purchase is one they meant to make.

Why the name works
Need+Value

Neeva combines the practical question of need with the longer-term question of value.

Colour direction 05 · Desire meets clarity

Coral asks the question. Teal answers it.

Two lead colours carry the idea, supported by soft surfaces and a deep slate for text. Click any swatch to copy its HEX.

Warm Coral

The spark of Need

Coral stands for the first attraction to a product. It is warm and noticeable without the aggression of a pure red. In Neeva, it invites the question: "Do I really need this?"

  • Warm and attention-grabbing
  • Reflects human desire and instinct
  • Marks the need-identification stage
Tidal Teal

The clarity of Value

Teal stands for evaluating what you already own, understanding cost per use and thinking about long-term usefulness. It brings a steadier visual experience once the shopping impulse has been interrupted.

  • Balanced and thoughtful
  • Contrasts the warmth of coral
  • Represents clarity and long-term value

Typography

A tall logotype, two working faces.

AM Tobruk is reserved for the wordmark. Manrope leads the interface, and IBM Plex Sans carries supporting and longer text.

LogotypeWordmark only

AM Tobruk

A condensed display face with a tall, open N that rises like a doorway. Its height lets the mascot stand on the letters in the lockup. Used only for the name, never for interface text.

Teal on light surfaces, Porcelain on Teal, Teal on Coral.

Manrope

How many times will you realistically use it?

Used for screen titles, questions, buttons and numbers. Its geometric shapes stay friendly at large sizes and clear at small ones.

A clearer picture for a brighter tomorrow. Price today, spent this month and expected use, laid out so the decision is easy to read.

Used for helper text, receipts, labels and long-form copy. Its open counters keep figures like ₹1,686 easy to scan.

User personas

Two shoppers, one pause.

We designed for college students whose purchases are driven by trends, sales and mood. Switch between them to see their empathy maps.

22 · Trend follower

Naksh

College student who follows fashion influencers and buys trending clothes to fit in and express his style.

Needs
  • Build a personal style
  • Find alternatives to buying new clothes
  • Make mindful shopping decisions
Motivation
  • Social acceptance and confidence
  • Expressing individuality
Pain points
  • Feels pressured to keep up with trends
  • Overspends on new styles
Where Neeva meets him

Question one asks what the purchase is for. It brings his own doubt, "Could I style what I already own?", to the surface before he pays.

Says

  • "Everyone is wearing this."
  • "I want to keep my style fresh."
  • "Is this brand worth the price?"

Thinks

  • "Will I feel left out if I don't get it?"
  • "Will I wear this after the trend fades?"
  • "Could I style what I already own?"

Does

  • Follows fashion creators
  • Saves trending outfits
  • Buys popular styles quickly

Feels

  • Excited by new drops
  • Pressure to fit in
  • Worried about missing out
21 · Impulse shopper

Riddhi

College student who enjoys online shopping and often buys clothes on the spot because of discounts, attractive designs and mood changes.

Needs
  • Pause and reconsider purchases
  • Make better use of existing clothes
  • Save money without giving up shopping
Motivation
  • Instant gratification
  • Finding good deals
  • Earning rewards for mindful choices
Pain points
  • Regrets unnecessary purchases
  • Has unworn clothes piling up
  • Finds it difficult to resist sales
Where Neeva meets her

The future receipt turns "I'll wear it someday" into a number of expected uses and a cost per wear. Her wish to earn rewards for mindful choices shaped our reward system.

Says

  • "It's on sale, so why not?"
  • "This is so cute!"
  • "I'll wear it someday."
  • "I deserve a little treat."

Thinks

  • "Will this look good on me?"
  • "What if the deal ends?"
  • "Do I really need this?"
  • "I can always return it."

Does

  • Browses shopping apps in her free time
  • Adds clothes to cart impulsively
  • Buys because of discounts or mood
  • Collects clothes she rarely wears

Feels

  • Excited while shopping
  • Tempted by limited-time offers
  • Regret after unnecessary purchases
  • Overwhelmed by a cluttered wardrobe
  • Guilty about wasting money and resources
How Neeva works

Six screens between "add to cart" and "pay".

Scroll to play the pop-up flow. The screens are drawn as wireframes in the Neeva palette, without copy, so the motion and structure stay in focus.

  1. 1Frame 1

    Neeva waits beside the cart

    A small coral bubble sits on the shopping app's cart screen. It stays quiet while the user browses and only invites a tap at checkout.

  2. 2Frame 2

    A gentle offer, not a block

    Tapping the bubble opens a card asking if the user wants a second perspective. The main action previews their future receipt; closing it returns them straight to the cart.

  3. 3Frame 3

    Question one: what is it for?

    A bottom sheet with four icon options names the purpose of the purchase in one tap. The two-part progress bar shows how short the check is.

  4. 4Frames 4, 7–10

    Question two: how often will you use it?

    Ranges replace exact numbers: 1–2, 3–5, 6–10+ or not sure. Each answer has its own selected state before the user continues.

  5. 5Frame 5

    The future receipt

    Today's price sits beside what was already spent this month and the new total. Dividing the price by expected uses gives a cost per wear.

  6. 6Frame 6

    The choice stays with the user

    Neeva records the decision and offers three equal exits: reconsider later, still buy it, or skip it for now. Nothing is blocked and nothing is judged.

Frame 1 of 6
Figma prototype

The wiring behind the pop-up.

Our prototype connects ten frames in two flows. Every answer on question two leads to its own selected state, so the prototype responds to the option a tester actually taps.

Flow 1

From the cart to the first question.

  1. Cart with the Neeva bubble
  2. "Want a second perspective?" card
  3. Question 1 of 2: what is it for
Flow 2

From usage to the decision.

  1. Question 2 of 2: expected uses
  2. Your future receipt with cost per wear
  3. Choice recorded, three exits

Frames 7–10 are the selected states for 1–2, 3–5, 6–10+ and Not sure.

Next · Reward system

Rewarding the pause, not the purchase.

Our next stage is a reward system that recognises mindful choices. These are our analogue sketches, followed by a first digital pass. The medals and rules below are proposals we are still testing.

Medal concept · from the sketch

The ₹3K month

A hexagonal medal awarded when a user saves ₹3,000 or more in a month by stepping back from carts after a Neeva check. The front carries a coral and teal swirl; the back records the amount saved that month.

Hover or tap the medal to flip it.

Worth it

Proposed · cost per wear

Inspiration we are drawing from: streaks in language-learning apps such as Duolingo, collectible badges in fitness trackers, and coin-style rewards in Indian fintech apps. Neeva adapts these so rewards follow reflection and good use, never spending.
